column1: #   One value, one DECLARATION, across the resolved MIOS_* environment that
#   usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot produces from the SSOT.  The resolver
#   traces every name to the SSOT key path whose value it carries
#   beside MIOS_CONVERGE_X, MIOS_PORT_X and MIOS_X_PORT beside MIOS_PORTS_X), a
#   port copied out of [ports.categories], a value that is only `${MIOS_X}`.
#   Names with one source are one declaration and never form a group; a group
#   is two or more DECLARATIONS sharing a value.  The tree violated that 816
#   times when this gate was written, so it RATCHETS rather than blocking:
#   every group that exists now is recorded below, one canonical name per
#   declaration, and the group count is pinned by the ceiling.
#   VIOLATION if a duplicate group appears whose value is not recorded here;
#   VIOLATION if a new declaration joins a group that is recorded here;
#   VIOLATION if the group count differs from the ceiling in either direction;
#   VIOLATION if the resolver, its provenance map, value-aliases.tsv, this
#   ledger, or python3 is missing or fails -- a gate with no data must never
#   report green, which is exactly how the previous version of this check
#   Do NOT add a row here to silence a new duplicate.  Collapse it: one key,
#   every consumer reading it (a `${MIOS_X}` reference is one declaration).
#   If the two keys really are DISTINCT FACTS that share a value by
#   coincidence -- either can change without the other becoming wrong -- that
#   has exactly one representation (task_942): a keep-distinct row in
#   already in the group, alias column = the newcomer, and the reason.
#   check_value_aliases proves the two are separate declarations and that the
#   reason is there; this gate then stops counting the newcomer.  Nothing else
#   #!ceiling is the number of groups and it is EXACT.  More groups is a
#   regression.  FEWER groups is also a failure, because a ceiling that never
#   comes down is how 816 accumulated: fixing duplicates must be paid for by
#   tightening this number in the same commit.
#   The ceiling lives here rather than in mios.toml because a number in the
#   SSOT that counts the resolved duplicate VALUES in the resolved environment is
#   self-referential -- "816" already occurs four times as an env value, so
#   declaring the ceiling in mios.toml would perturb the very set it counts.
# REGENERATE (after a legitimate SSOT change, and review the diff)
#   declaration (its canonical spelling), ordered by descending count then
#   value.  The value field escapes backslash as \, TAB as \t
#   and CR as \r.  Values the gate does not treat as duplicates at all --
#   the empty string, true/false, 0/1 and the well-known ports 22/53/80/443/
